The decision to mark body, limb, tail, and gait checkpoints as 'is_testable: false' is logically sound given the tight cropping of the image; these features are genuinely occluded or out-of-frame. I agree with all verdicts. The Router was not too lenient; it strictly adhered to visibility constraints.
artifact_review: The Router flagged a texture anomaly in the collar (severity 1.5) and slight edge blending in the ears (severity 0.5). The Perceptual Quality Auditor found no graphics-level distortions (noise/blur), which contradicts the severity of the Router's collar claim slightly, but the 'mushy' pattern description is plausible for AI generations struggling with complex textures on curved surfaces. The Animal Pose Auditor reported a HIGH artifact risk due to low-confidence keypoints in the hind limbs and one ear. However, since the hind limbs are out of frame, those low confidences are expected (domain shift/occlusion). The low confidence in the Left Ear (0.43) coincides with the Router's observation of edge softness. I will maintain the Router's artifact findings but treat the pose auditor's limb warnings as false positives due to cropping. The collar issue is the primary structural/textural defect.
